# Updates and versions

## What it is

Hive is tested against specific versions of opencode, oh-my-openagent and OpenSpec. A Hive release pins those versions, and `habithive update` brings your machine to the release you install. Hive also checks once a day for a newer release and tells you inside opencode. Nothing updates on its own.

## The daily update check

When the Hive plugin loads, it reads a cache (`~/.habithive/update-check.json`). If a newer release is known, opencode shows a toast: `habithive v<version> available — quit and run habithive update`. At most one such toast appears per process.

The cache refreshes in the background from the public npm registry when the last success is over 24 hours old and the last attempt over 1 hour old. The check has a 3-second timeout, never blocks startup and is silent on failure.

## `habithive update`

Quit opencode first, then run:

```bash
habithive update
```

Steps:

1. Checks npm for the latest `habithive-code`.
2. If it is newer than the installed version, runs `npm i -g habithive-code@latest`. If npm is unreachable it says so and reconciles the installed version. If the install fails, check npm's global prefix permissions and retry.
3. Runs the **new version's** `reconcile --yes` so its pins apply, not the old ones.
4. Prints `restart opencode to load habithive v<version>`.

Update keeps your mode, model overrides and config. It does not record a mode or rename files.

If you run Hive from a source checkout, `habithive update` does not overwrite it from npm. It prints `update it with: git -C <path> pull && habithive update` and reconciles the checkout.

## `habithive reconcile`

Reconcile is `setup` without the mode change. It is hidden from `--help` and is what `update` runs. Use it after pulling a source checkout or when you want to re-apply pins:

```bash
habithive reconcile          # prompts before installing opencode if it is missing
habithive reconcile --yes    # no prompts
```

It runs these steps, applied to **every mode set that exists** (see [02-modes.md](02-modes.md)):

| Step | Action |
|------|--------|
| 1 | Install opencode at the pin, or move an existing 1.x install to it (`npm i -g opencode-ai@<pin>` for an npm install, `opencode upgrade <pin>` otherwise) |
| 2 | Wire the Hive plugin (both sets) and oh-my-openagent (complex set only); replace stale entries |
| 3 | Set `autoupdate: false` in each `opencode.jsonc` |
| 4 | Reset Hive-owned OmniRoute values in each set ([04-omniroute.md](04-omniroute.md)) |
| 5 | Add the Playwright MCP server if absent |
| 6 | Install OpenSpec at its pin and the intent-driven schema |
| 7 | Install or upgrade graphify |
| 8 | Copy the bundled skills into `~/.config/opencode/skills/` |

## Pinned versions

These are set in `src/versions.js` and move only with a Hive release.

| Tool | Constant | Value |
|------|----------|-------|
| opencode | `OPENCODE_PIN` | 1.19.4 |
| oh-my-openagent | `OMO_SPEC` | `oh-my-openagent@4.19.1` |
| OpenSpec | `OPENSPEC_PIN` | 1.5.0 |
| Node.js | `NODE_MIN` | 20.19.0 (minimum, not an exact pin) |

Why they are pinned: oh-my-openagent 5.x moves the config file Hive manages, and newer OpenSpec releases reject the intent-driven schema. The test evidence for each pin is in [../COMPATIBILITY.md](../COMPATIBILITY.md).

### What floats

| Tool | Behavior |
|------|----------|
| graphify | Upgraded to the latest release by `update` and `reconcile` (via `uv`, else `pip` on Python 3.10+) |
| Playwright MCP | Wired as `@playwright/mcp@latest`; npx fetches the current version |

## Why `autoupdate` is false

Hive writes `"autoupdate": false` in `opencode.jsonc` in both mode sets. opencode therefore never upgrades itself to a version Hive has not tested. opencode moves only when you run `habithive update` or `habithive setup`.

## Drift warnings

If the opencode on your machine differs from `OPENCODE_PIN`, Hive warns:

- At launch (shell): `opencode <version> is not the tested 1.19.4 — run: habithive update`
- Inside opencode, if started without the launcher: a toast saying the same.

The launch still continues. Run `habithive update` to move to the pin.

## OpenCode 2 guard

Hive needs OpenCode 1. On OpenCode 2, complex mode and the model tree do not work. If Hive detects a different major version it prints a red notice at launch, in `habithive status`, and during `setup`/`update`, then continues. It does not try to downgrade (OpenCode 2 cannot be downgraded with `opencode upgrade`).

Recovery depends on how you installed OpenCode 2. Hive detects the method and prints one of these:

```bash
# npm
npm rm -g @opencode/cli
habithive setup

# Homebrew
brew uninstall opencode-v2
habithive setup

# curl installer
curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash -s -- --version 1.19.4
```

If the method is not detected, Hive lists all three. Sessions created under OpenCode 2 may not open in OpenCode 1.

# 8. Files and safety

## What it is

This chapter lists every file and folder Hive reads or writes, the guarantees around those writes, and how to remove Hive completely. Paths use `~` for your home directory.

## Files Hive writes

### opencode config (`~/.config/opencode/`)

| File | Written by | What changes |
|------|------------|--------------|
| `opencode.jsonc` | setup, update, `--gateway` | `plugin` (oh-my-openagent in complex mode), `autoupdate: false`, `mcp.playwright` (only if absent), `provider.omniroute` |
| `tui.json` | setup, update | The Hive plugin `file://` entry in `plugin` |
| `opencode.json` | setup, update | Only if it already lists oh-my-openagent: it is then part of the mode set and handled like the files above |
| `oh-my-openagent.json` | model tree | Agent and category models. Not live: applies on relaunch |
| `skills/<name>/` | setup, update | Copies of the bundled skills |
| `<file>.habithive-bak-<timestamp>` | any edit above | Backup made before a change |

During a mode switch these config files are also renamed, not edited (see below).

### Hive store (`~/.habithive/`)

| Path | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `mode` | The active mode (`simple` or `complex`) |
| `modes/<mode>/` | The inactive mode's stored config set |
| `modes/files.json` | Which file names make up a mode set |
| `switch.journal` | Present only during a mode switch, so an interrupted switch can finish or roll back |
| `overrides.json` | Your model choices from the model tree |
| `baseline.json` | Snapshot of your original `oh-my-openagent.json`, restored by Reset |
| `oh-my-openagent.first-backup.json` | Byte copy of that original file |
| `last-applied.sha256` | Hash of the `oh-my-openagent.json` text Hive last wrote, to tell its writes from yours |
| `pending-apply.json` | A main-agent model change waiting to be applied after relaunch |
| `next-mode`, `next-session` | Queued in-app mode switch and the session to reopen; cleared on launch |
| `update-check.json` | Cache of the daily "new release?" check against the npm registry |
| `schema-installed.sha256` | Hash of the `intent-driven` schema Hive last installed |
| `schema-backups/` | Your edited schema copy, kept here when setup replaces it |

### Elsewhere

| Path | What Hive does |
|------|----------------|
| `~/.local/share/openspec/schemas/intent-driven` | Installs the schema (the base follows `XDG_DATA_HOME` or `LOCALAPPDATA` when set) |
| `~/.local/state/opencode/model.json` | On a main-agent model change, moves the old and new model to the front of `recent` |
| `<project>/openspec/`, `<project>/.opencode/` | Created by `hive spec init` |

Hive also reads opencode's session list and the `opencode --version` output; it writes nothing there.

## Safety guarantees

- A normal launch never writes config. `habithive status` reads only `~/.habithive/mode`.
- A mode switch only renames files. The first switch to a mode creates its set once from the active files; after that, contents are never edited.
- Switches are journaled. A launch finishes or rolls back an interrupted switch before doing anything else.
- Only `habithive setup`, `habithive update` and `habithive --gateway` edit your config.
- Every edit goes through one safe-edit routine: it parses the file first, makes no write when nothing changes, saves `<file>.habithive-bak-<timestamp>` next to the file, writes through a temp file and rename, keeps the file's permissions, and keeps only the newest 5 backups per file.
- An edited file is saved as plain JSON. Every setting is kept, but comments and layout are not; the backup keeps the original.
- If a file cannot be parsed, Hive writes nothing and prints `cannot read <file>:<line>:<col>`. Fix the file and re-run.
- Hive refuses to apply model overrides over an empty baseline, so it cannot wipe oh-my-openagent's config.
- Hive never writes API keys.

Never touched: your keys, other providers, sessions, projects, models you added to OmniRoute, and any config value Hive does not manage.

## Uninstall

Switch to the mode whose config you want to keep, because deleting `~/.habithive` removes the other mode's stored set.

```sh
habithive complex                                      # or: habithive simple
npm rm -g habithive-code
npm rm -g @fission-ai/openspec                         # optional: the pinned OpenSpec CLI
rm -rf ~/.local/share/openspec/schemas/intent-driven   # optional: the schema
rm -rf ~/.habithive
rm -f ~/.config/opencode/*.habithive-bak-*             # optional: backups
```

Then remove the Hive plugin and `oh-my-openagent` entries from `~/.config/opencode/tui.json` and `opencode.jsonc`, and the `omniroute` provider if you do not want it. Also optional: `~/.config/opencode/skills/` copies, the `playwright` MCP entry, and `"autoupdate": false` (opencode then updates itself again). Project folders created by `hive spec init` stay.

# 9. Troubleshooting

## What it is

Each entry is a symptom, the cause Hive's code handles, and the fix. `hive` is the same command as `habithive`. Hive prints `!` lines for warnings and keeps going; it only stops on a config parse error or a failed install.

## Models and relaunch

### The model did not change on screen

Cause: only main-agent and Everything changes move the on-screen model, and only through a relaunch. Subagent, sub-agent group and tier changes are saved to `oh-my-openagent.json` and apply on relaunch; the agent on screen keeps its model. If the automatic step cannot run, opencode's model picker opens and a toast names the model to select.

Fix: select the model in the picker, or relaunch with `habithive -c`. See [Model tree](03-model-tree.md).

### "waiting for the open prompt"

Cause: a permission or question prompt is open. Hive does not quit opencode while one is open, because quitting would reject it.

Fix: answer the prompt. The change then applies. If opencode does not quit within 3 seconds, type `/exit` so the launcher can reopen the session.

### "saved - restart with `habithive -c` to apply"

Cause: opencode was started as plain `opencode`, not through `habithive`, so there is no launcher to relaunch it. The change is saved.

Fix: quit and run `habithive -c`.

### Another mode's provider or MCP server is missing

Cause: each mode keeps its own complete config set; changes made in one mode are not in the other.

Fix: copy the entry from `~/.habithive/modes/<mode>/` (the inactive set) into the active file. See [Modes](02-modes.md).

## Versions

### "opencode X is not the tested Y"

Cause: the installed opencode differs from the version pinned in this Hive release.

Fix: run `habithive update`. It moves opencode to the pin (`npm i -g opencode-ai@<pin>` for an npm install, `opencode upgrade <pin>` otherwise). `habithive setup` does the same.

### "Upgrade failed: Unknown installation method"

Cause: Hive 0.3.0 moved opencode with `opencode upgrade`, which gives up on npm installs under Homebrew's Node (`/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules`). From 0.3.1, Hive uses npm for those.

Fix: run `habithive update`, or move opencode yourself with `npm i -g opencode-ai@1.19.4`.

### OpenCode 2 detected

Cause: OpenCode 2 is installed (for example through `opencode upgrade --major`). Complex mode and the model tree do not work on it.

Fix: go back to OpenCode 1 with the command for your install method, then run `habithive setup` where shown. The launcher, `habithive status` and `habithive setup` print the right commands; see the Compatibility section of the [README](../../README.md#compatibility). Never run `opencode upgrade --major`.

### "habithive needs Node.js 20.19 or newer"

Cause: Node is older than 20.19 (OpenSpec requires it).

Fix: `nvm install 22`, then retry.

### "graphify needs uv (brew install uv) or Python 3.10+; skipped"

Cause: graphify needs Python 3.10+. There is no `uv`, Python is older (macOS's built-in one is 3.9), and Homebrew is not installed, so setup cannot install `uv` for you.

Fix: install `uv` (`brew install uv`, or see the uv documentation), then run `habithive setup` again.

### "graphify is installed but not on your PATH"

Cause: `uv` installs tools into `~/.local/bin`, which is not on every PATH.

Fix: run `uv tool update-shell`, then open a new terminal.

### `npm i -g` fails with `EACCES`

Cause: npm's global prefix is not writable. Fix: use a user-owned prefix or nvm, never `sudo`. See [Getting started](01-getting-started.md#install).

## Config files

### "cannot read <file>:<line>:<col>"

Cause: a config file Hive must edit has a syntax error. Hive writes nothing in that case.

Fix: open the file at that line and column, fix it, re-run the command.

## OmniRoute

### "connection refused" from OmniRoute

Cause: OmniRoute is not enabled. The provider points at the placeholder `http://localhost:20128/v1` until you set a gateway.

Fix: run `habithive --gateway <ip>`, then `/connect` in opencode to add your key. `habithive update` never changes the address. See [OmniRoute](04-omniroute.md).

### OmniRoute sends no key

Cause: an older hand-copied OmniRoute block has `"apiKey": "{env:OMNIROUTE_API_KEY}"` and that variable is unset. opencode then sends no key and ignores the one saved by `/connect`. Hive never adds or removes that line.

Fix: export `OMNIROUTE_API_KEY`, or delete that line from the `omniroute` provider block.

## Plugin and launcher

### Two wordmarks on the home screen

Cause: the previous package is still wired into a global or per-project opencode config.

Fix: follow [Migrating from the previous package name](01-getting-started.md#migrating-from-the-previous-package-name).

### "habithive plugin path is stale"

Cause: `tui.json` names a Hive plugin path that no longer exists, for example after the global npm install moved.

Fix: run `habithive setup`. It replaces the stale entry.

### `hive` runs a different program

Cause: another program named `hive` (such as Apache Hive) is earlier on your PATH. Setup warns about this.

Fix: use `habithive`, which is the same command.

## Specs

### The schema is missing in a project

Cause: the project has OpenSpec set up with another schema, or its `openspec/schemas/intent-driven` copy is gone. `hive spec init` leaves an initialized project alone and prints how to switch.

Fix: run `habithive setup` to reinstall the user-level schema, then in the project:

```sh
openspec schema fork intent-driven intent-driven
```

and set `schema: intent-driven` in `openspec/config.yaml`. To refresh an existing copy: `rm -rf openspec/schemas/intent-driven && openspec schema fork intent-driven intent-driven`. If `hive spec init` says "openspec not found", run `habithive setup`. See [Spec workflow](05-spec-workflow.md).
